spec.title: JBMC's escaping exceptions named and refused: corpus under JBMC, auto and --confirm, and the integration tests (engine-priorities step 3)
spec.description: Step 3 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. JBMC's counterexamples to conformance/caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 (n=0) did not reproduce, because JBMC 6.11.0 lets a runtime exception past the handler that catches it on the JVM, in two shapes (lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/README.md). (1) return-past-handler, a JBMC defect: for 'try { return 10 / n; } catch (ArithmeticException e)', javac ends the handler's range before ireturn, and JBMC computes the quotient and its division-by-zero check at the ireturn, after pop_catch. (2) stubbed-handler: JBMC's stub of a JDK exception class has no superclass, so 'catch (RuntimeException e)' misses an ArithmeticException or IllegalArgumentException. Both also gave false proofs under strict with --engine jbmc (caught and a new method caughtAsRuntime, with --throws 'ArithmeticException when n == 0', where the JVM returns -1). The JBMC preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs, Defect) now finds both shapes in the bytecode JBMC reaches and refuses a JBMC proof through one under every gap mode; a counterexample is still replayed, and its message names the defect. The corpus gains conformance/caught/3, caughtAsRuntime/1 and caughtAsRuntime/2 (checked on the JVM inline, with the own checker). This job runs what needs JBMC: the integration tests, and the ignored conformance tests under --engine jbmc and auto (strict) and under auto --confirm (strict and assume). Steps run on even if one fails. Known on cvm: the JDK is 25.0.5 and the contract library's records are 25.0.4.1, which fails advised runs that use the library (the inline own-checker conformance test has 12 such disagreements); the steps here are strict and assume, but an integration test under advised may meet it.
spec.expected: Each step exits 0. Under --engine jbmc, conformance/caught/3 and caughtAsRuntime/2 are no verdict (the proof refused, naming return-past-handler and stubbed-handler), caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 unverifiable with the defect named as the cause; under auto all four are decided by the own checker. A claim JBMC says Verified that the JVM refutes is a finding to triage, as is any integration test that now fails because a JBMC proof it expects is refused for a defect.
